x-jsf-presentation.description:
In this section, you can select the benefits you'll provide to your new team member. If you already employ team members in the same country, your new hire will receive the same benefits to ensure consistency and compliance with our benefit equality policy.

If this is your first hire in the country, the options you select below will become the standard for any future hires in that location.

Important for Germany:
Team members in Germany have a legal right to contribute a portion of their gross salary to a company pension scheme (bAV), also known as deferred compensation.
Employers are legally required to offer access to this plan upon employee request and must contribute an additional 15% subsidy (up to €45/month) on top of the employee's monthly contribution.
The "Minimum" plan fulfills the legal requirement.
x-jsf-presentation.extra: Prices are listed in U.S. Dollars (USD). However, when benefits are originally priced in local currencies, these amounts are estimates in USD. The final charge in local currency will be determined using the exchange rate at the time of invoicing. The pricing listed is subject to change based on the age of the employee (age banding) and/or plan changes/renewals. Any pricing changes will be communicated in advance.

statement.description:
If you need Remote to terminate a post-probation employee in Germany because of your company’s economic or organizational circumstances, a mutual termination agreement must be entered into with the employee. Performance-related terminations must meet a high threshold of compliance.

It is common for employees in Germany to bring claims and employers to pay settlements or to opt for termination by mutual agreement.

During probation, you have some more flexibility on termination; for example, when the termination reason is the employee’s performance. For this reason, we recommend setting the probation period to the maximum allowed.
